clue.text: Harold is reported to have done this in Scottish town

indicators.note: is reported says the action described is to be heard spoken, not spelt, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: King Harold II fought William the Conqueror at the Battle of Hastings in 1066, so what Harold did was fight William

explanation.surface: A gossip claims King Harold once did something in a Highland town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harold' points to the English king killed at Hastings in 1066 by William's invading army; 'fought William' said out loud matches the town's name. Fort William is a town in the western Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Fort William is a town at the foot of Ben Nevis in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Distress for conservatives stuck in marsh

indicators.note: stuck in places the word for conservatives inside the word for a marsh

parts.note: a fen is a low wet marsh, as in the East Anglian Fens
the political right means conservatives

explanation.surface: Tories are upset at being bogged down in a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: To distress someone is to alarm or scare them, the verb sense.

clue.text: One of the family about to reject very important point

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: to reject throws the word back, so the synonym for very important is read backwards

parts.note: vital means very important
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A relative is poised to dismiss a key argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reject' turns VITAL into LATIV, which sits between RE and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a kinsman, someone in your family.

clue.text: Charming woman ambition

definitions.note: used as a noun, a person who does charming in the magical sense, casting spells

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving or ambition

explanation.surface: An attractive lady with high aspirations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming woman' reads as one phrase, but 'woman' supplies W, leaving 'Charming' as the definition in the sense of working charms or spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts charms, that is spells, so she is one who practises charming.

clue.text: Putting mind at rest about injury in organ

indicators.note: in puts the reversed injury word inside the word for an organ

parts.note: the lung is a breathing organ

indicators.note: about turns the word for injury round

parts.note: an ill is a harm or injury

explanation.surface: Reassuring a patient about damage to a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ILL into LLI, which goes inside LUNG after LU.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulling someone is soothing them into calm, settling their fears.

clue.text: Understanding fashionable view

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a sight is a view, something seen

explanation.surface: A grasp of what is in vogue to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception or grasp of something.

clue.text: Systems manager in a state about female memory

indicators.note: about puts the US state round the other letters

parts.note: Maine is a US state
RAM is computer memory, random access memory

explanation.surface: An IT boss in some American state worries over a woman's recollection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Systems manager' sounds like a job title, but it is a large central computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainframe is a big central computer that runs an organisation's systems.

clue.text: Almost manage to capture

indicators.note: almost means the word is one letter short of complete, losing its last

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Nearly succeeding in catching someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop is slang for to catch or seize.

clue.text: Plump fish, black, unknown

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A fat fish, dark in colour and of no known species.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means rounded and fleshy, a synonym of plump.

clue.text: Muddles about church articles

indicators.note: about makes the word for muddles go round the church letters

parts.note: pie, also pi, is a jumbled mess, originally of printer's type
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Confusion over religious newspaper features.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces are items or articles, as in pieces of writing or furniture.

clue.text: One's allowed an inch

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A person is permitted just a little leeway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' is not the measure here: in Scotland an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a small island, which is what a Scottish inch is.

clue.text: Weariness of girl I played duet with

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: played means the letters are performed in a new order

explanation.surface: Tiredness felt by a young woman after a duet together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges I and DUET into ITUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness and lack of energy.

clue.text: Produce young fish; a very young one

parts.note: to hatch is to bring forth young from eggs
the ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Breeding fish, starting with a baby one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchling is a baby bird or reptile just out of the egg.

clue.text: Flaubert's first clever story

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the French novelist's name

parts.note: able means clever, capable

explanation.surface: Flaubert's earliest tale was a smart piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short moral tale, often with animal characters.

clue.text: Last two men in competition begrudging others success

indicators.note: last two picks the final pair of letters of the word that follows

parts.note: vying means competing, being in competition

explanation.surface: The final pair of male contestants resent each other's wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Envying is resenting someone else's good fortune or achievements.

clue.text: Urge a Parisian to follow meaning

indicators.note: to follow places the French article after the word for meaning

parts.note: import means meaning or significance
une is French for a, the feminine form a Parisian would use

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman is pushed to fall in line with the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to press or pester someone persistently.

clue.text: Shop around for transport

indicators.note: around turns the word for a shop backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market or shop

explanation.surface: Browsing a store in search of a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a streetcar, a means of public transport.

clue.text: Most agile man's ending with badly set limb

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of the word for man
badly signals the following words are put together wrong, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: The quickest player has a broken arm poorly reset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges SET LIMB into IMBLEST, after N from 'man's ending'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimblest is the superlative of nimble, meaning quickest and lightest on one's feet.

clue.text: Count supporting first lady's return? Hardly!

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the second word below the first
return reads the possessive name of the first woman backwards

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis, and the 's adds S
to count on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A nobleman holds up a returning first lady's train, though barely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman but is the verb, 'rely'. 'Hardly' is not 'barely' here; it is 'in a hard way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly in its old sense means harshly, in a hard manner, which is what severely means.

clue.text: Describe endlessly; it's a long story

indicators.note: endlessly removes the first and last letters of the verb

parts.note: to depict is to describe or portray

explanation.surface: A storyteller describes things that go on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or saga.

clue.text: Heartless girl turns up with drink supplier

parts.note: cold means unfeeling, heartless

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue reads the girl's name upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Pat is a girl's name, short for Patricia

explanation.surface: An unfeeling woman arrives with a bottle-provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like a deletion signal, but it is COLD, unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A tap supplies water to drink, and this is the one for unheated water.

clue.text: Plaster, I learn, has to be extremely clean

indicators.note: has signals the run of letters is held inside the words plaster, I learn

explanation.surface: A student is told plaster must be kept spotless.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means free of germs, completely clean in a surgical sense.

clue.text: Escorted second queen back into pound

indicators.note: into places the reversed queen inside the word for a pound

parts.note: a quid is British slang for a pound sterling

indicators.note: back turns the queen's letters round

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A second monarch is returned to the animal pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ER into RE, which goes inside QUID; QUID is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To squire someone is to escort or attend them, like a knight's attendant.

clue.text: Water board puts theologian in post

indicators.note: in places the theologian's letters inside the word for post

parts.note: a pale is a fence stake or post
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: The utility company appoints a religious scholar to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water board' suggests a utility firm; it is the flat blade pushed through water.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle is a flat-bladed oar, a board for propelling a canoe through water.

clue.text: Discuss using northern force

annotationWithheld.why: Discuss using northern force (6) for CONFER: no reading found giving C-O-N-F-E-R from 'using', 'northern' and 'force'; the OCR text may be wrong and no blog or database gives the clue

clue.text: After a short time one of us has royal affair

indicators.note: after places the last two pieces behind the short time

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: one of takes a single letter, the first, from the word us

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: After a brief while a member of our group has a fling with a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: It's silly to organise a huge ball

indicators.note: to organise means the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: It is ridiculous to throw an enormous dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughable means ridiculous, so absurd it invites laughter.

clue.text: River water around bay?

indicators.note: around puts the word for water round the river letter

parts.note: to hose is to water, as a garden

explanation.surface: A river's waters swirl round a coastal inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' is not a coastal inlet but a reddish-brown horse; the question mark admits it is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay is a brown-coated horse, so a bay is an example of the animal.

clue.text: One not settling fuel trade arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A party that fails to honour a fuel deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges FUEL TRADE; 'settling' means paying a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A defaulter is someone who fails to pay what they owe.

clue.text: Steward is substitute when listed openers are dropped

indicators.note: are dropped removes the named letters from the word for substitute

parts.note: to relieve is to take over from, stand in as a substitute
the opening letters of listed, its first two, are L and I

explanation.surface: A manager stands in when the scheduled opening batsmen are left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' sounds like cricket batsmen, but it is the start of 'listed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a manor's chief officer, a magistrate or bailiff acting as steward.

clue.text: Nobleman without money gets attention

indicators.note: without removes the money letter from the nobleman

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
L is the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A penniless aristocrat is noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to give them attention, a hearing.

clue.text: Former partner typed line out in a helpful way

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An ex-husband typed a line out to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Expediently means in a way that serves the purpose, conveniently.
